clue.text: Wall painting survives, higher

parts.note: to survive is to last, so 'survives' gives lasts
higher means upper

explanation.surface: A mural has lasted, and hangs higher up the wall than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wall painting' sounds generic, but it points to Leonardo's famous fresco in Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci's Last Supper is a celebrated mural painted on a refectory wall in Milan.

clue.text: Work of editor extremely desirable

indicators.note: to work something is to shape it anew, so the letters following are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor's piece of work is highly sought after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like a noun, but it is the anagram signal on OF EDITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something you would die for is so wanted that it is irresistible, an idiom for great desirability.

clue.text: Relaxing in an exam covering one of the three basics?

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A

indicators.note: covering means the exam words wrap around the basic letter placed within

parts.note: an exam is a test
the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic) are the basics of schooling, so one is R

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm during a test on reading, writing or arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'three Rs' are reading, 'riting and 'rithmetic, the traditional school basics.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at rest is to be in repose, idle and calm, which is relaxing.

clue.text: Leave, almost completely

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short, losing its final letter

parts.note: quite can mean completely, as in 'quite right'

explanation.surface: Someone is leaving, or nearly finished leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit a place or job is to depart from it, a direct synonym for leave.

clue.text: Conflicted, paired off to maintain attention

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the paired words hold the attention word inside them

parts.note: things paired off are arranged in twos
to mind something is to attend to it, so mind is attention

explanation.surface: Pupils split into pairs to keep them concentrating feel torn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to maintain' puts MIND inside IN TWOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being undecided between two choices is an idiom for feeling torn, unable to settle.

clue.text: Sudden chill: mild illnesses need sleep

parts.note: colds are minor ailments
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A cold spell means people with sniffles need rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold snap is a brief spell of unusually cold weather that arrives abruptly.

clue.text: Two bottles unfinished? This situation benefits us both

indicators.note: Two means the trimmed word appears twice in a row
unfinished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: bottles here stands for their contents, wine

explanation.surface: Two half-drunk bottles of wine make everyone happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts WINE to WIN, and 'Two' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A win-win outcome is one where every party gains, so both sides come out ahead.

clue.text: Woman's meeting daughter in crowd

parts.note: her is the possessive of a woman

explanation.surface: A woman meets her daughter in a busy throng.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a large group, often of animals, used loosely of a mass of people too.

clue.text: Change after a boxing match, as soldiers may be ordered

indicators.note: after puts the change word behind the boxing words in the answer

parts.note: a bout is a boxing contest
to turn is to change

explanation.surface: A boxer changes course after a fight, as if drilled on the parade ground.
explanation.walkthrough: An about-turn is a drill command telling soldiers to face the opposite way.
explanation.definitionFit: On the parade ground soldiers are commanded to reverse direction with this drill order.

clue.text: Give one's view, nothing long

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
to long for something is to pine for it

explanation.surface: Someone offers an opinion that amounts to nothing much.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, a formal verb for expressing what you think.

clue.text: Travel protected by explosive weapon

indicators.note: protected by means the travel word is surrounded by the explosive

parts.note: TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene
to ride is to travel

explanation.surface: A journey guarded by an explosive device.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, the weapon of Neptune and of Roman gladiators.

clue.text: With words of acceptance, married: later so alone

parts.note: I do is the vow spoken when accepting a spouse
to be wed is to be married

explanation.surface: A marriage vow, a wedding, and eventually solitude.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface follows a marriage from vow to bereavement; the definition is its sad end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose spouse has died is left without a partner, single again after marriage.

clue.text: Needing exercise, one circles a furlong

indicators.note: circles means the word for one goes round the furlong letter

parts.note: a unit is one
F is the abbreviation for furlong in horse racing

explanation.surface: An out-of-shape runner does laps of a furlong.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out of condition, lacking fitness, would benefit from a workout.

clue.text: Control working and income

indicators.note: working here means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Holding down a job and earning money gives you power.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominance is power or authority over others, which is mastery or control.

clue.text: Record how old we are to dampen enthusiasm

parts.note: a record is a disc
how old we are is our age

explanation.surface: Writing down our age is enough to deflate us.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone is to dishearten them, sapping their eagerness or keenness.

clue.text: Road sorely in need of repair sooner than usual

indicators.note: something in need of repair is broken, so these letters are put back together differently

explanation.surface: A road badly needs fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: EARLY DOORS is British informal speech, originally from pub opening times, for early on.
explanation.definitionFit: This British informal phrase means early on, at an earlier stage than normal.

clue.text: Gun shop price war may show value of money

indicators.note: may show suggests the letters can be rearranged to display another phrase

explanation.surface: A price war among gun shops reveals what money is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchasing power is the amount of goods a unit of currency can buy, its real worth.

clue.text: Awkward person playing charades

indicators.note: playing suggests letters at play, moved about into another order

explanation.surface: Someone who is being difficult during a game of charades.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard case is a tough, difficult or obstinate individual.

clue.text: Sort of brief observation

definitions.meaning: a ... brief is a lawyer's instruction to follow a case on a client's behalf

explanation.surface: A short note on what someone has seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Watching is keeping an eye on things, while a watching brief is a legal remit to monitor.

clue.text: Prepare war orders for Flying Squad

indicators.note: to prepare is to make ready, so these letters are made up into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting military commands ready for the police's elite unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Flying Squad is a London police unit; here it means the Red Arrows, the RAF's aerobatic display team.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Arrows are the Royal Air Force display team, literally a squad that flies.

clue.text: Is very nervous of locks

definitions.meaning: to dread something is to fear it greatly
short for dreadlocks, matted ropes of hair

explanation.surface: Someone is frightened of their door locks.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreads means fears, and is also the informal word for dreadlocks, a hairstyle.

clue.text: Wait to eat a Malaysian dish

indicators.note: to eat is to take in, so the wait word swallows the article

parts.note: to stay is to wait, remaining where you are

explanation.surface: Someone waits patiently before tucking into a meal from Malaysia.
explanation.definitionFit: Satay is skewered grilled meat with peanut sauce, a staple of Malaysian and Indonesian cooking.

clue.text: Opening foreign letter with edge of thumb makes bad mark

indicators.note: opening means the letter is cut open so the thumb's edge can enter

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: edge of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Slitting an envelope from abroad with a thumbnail leaves a smudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' puts T, the 'edge of thumb', inside SIGMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace, figuratively a stain on someone's reputation.

clue.text: Went for a drive; may it have been clocked?

definitions.text: Went for a drive; may it have been clocked?

parts.words: Went for a drive; may it have been clocked?
parts.note: 'Went for a drive' reads as a trip out but means employed for driving; clocking is illegally winding back a car's mileage reading

explanation.surface: Someone took a car out and wonders if a speed camera caught them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clocked' suggests caught speeding, but in the motor trade it means the odometer was tampered with, a classic risk with second-hand vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-hand car has been driven before, and its mileage may have been falsified.

clue.text: Tongue's fur due for scraping

indicators.note: scraping takes off the outside, leaving the inner letters of these words

explanation.surface: A furry tongue is ready for a scrape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' looks like a body part, but it is a language; scraping the ends off FUR DUE leaves it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means language, and Urdu is the national language of Pakistan.

clue.text: Explosion, after which children all fall down?

definitions.text: Explosion, after which children all fall down?

parts.words: Explosion, after which children all fall down?
parts.note: the nursery rhyme Ring a Ring o' Roses ends with a sneeze, then 'we all fall down'; a sneeze is a nasal explosion

explanation.surface: A blast knocks a group of children off their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosion' suggests a bomb, but it is a sneeze from the playground rhyme Ring a Ring o' Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the sound of a sneeze, sung just before the children drop to the ground.

clue.text: In the car, I take the wheel

definitions.text: In the car, I take the wheel

parts.words: In the car, I take the wheel
parts.note: 'take the wheel' suggests driving, but here it is a part that literally holds the wheels

explanation.surface: A passenger offers to do the driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take the wheel' means drive, but the speaker is a car part on which wheels are mounted.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the shaft on which a vehicle's wheels turn, so it bears them.

clue.text: English in clothes for stylish people

indicators.note: in means the English letter is placed inside the clothes word

parts.note: duds is slang for clothes

explanation.surface: An Englishman in his outfit among fashionable folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Dude originally meant a dandy, a man very concerned with fashion and appearance.

clue.text: One in a rush to claim riches involved demon girl

definitions.text: One in a rush to claim riches

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: A wicked girl is mixed up in a scramble for wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush' is a gold rush, a stampede to newly found goldfields.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospector who joined a gold rush hoped to stake a claim and get rich.
